reasoning.text: The agent initially identified the correct target file and existing audit tests, but its first implementation grouped vulnerabilities by identical complete identifier sets rather than by any shared identifier, which did not satisfy the specification [T0B11:<RANGE>Algorithm: for each result, compute a "signature" set = {id} | aliases. Use a dict from frozenset(signature) -> merged result.</RANGE>]. It later changed to a union-find approach and got the focused audit tests passing [T0B90:<RANGE>10 passed, 3 warnings in 0.01s</RANGE>], and its manual examples produced the expected output [T0B92:<RANGE>Ex1: 1 [('PYSEC-0', {'GHSA-aaaa', 'CVE-2024-0001'})]</RANGE>] [T0B92:<RANGE>Ex2: 1 [('PYSEC-0', {'GHSA-aaaa', 'CVE-2024-0001'})]</RANGE>]. However, the implementation's grouping logic remains suspect because it stores vulnerability objects in groups but checks roots using positional indices over each group's length rather than preserving original indices [T0B89:<RANGE>if any(find(j) == root for j in range(len(group))):</RANGE>], so hidden cases could be incorrectly grouped. The run also exhausted its budget after repeated malformed or redundant terminal interactions, and the full suite had eight failures [T0B98:<RANGE>8 failed, 231 passed, 3 warnings in 131.88s (0:02:11)</RANGE>].
